judgement.rule: A unit's GW points are its datasheet's band for that copy and size, plus each of GW's WARGEAR OPTIONS costs its selections take, plus its enhancement's. A selection takes the wargear row of its own name, or of each item of a bundle it names (split on '&', ',' or 'and'), names compared in the singular (New Recruit's 'Twin Killsaw' takes GW's 'per Twin Killsaws 5'), each row once on a selection's path. One matcher: verify/points.js (the gate step points) prices a list's wargear with builder.js wargearOf, no copy of its own.

where: verify/build-parity.js N (GW's wargear costs; the Shield-Captain cases; the Meganobz case)

judgement.rule: The paid-wargear check is against GW's rows only, DATASHEETS points.wargear (held to the Wahapedia page's 'per <item> N' rows by verify/catalog.js texts): every row is taken through wargearOf by at least one wargear choice of its datasheet, and no choice takes a row whose item its name does not name (the name or an item of a bundle, in the singular). No price of New Recruit's or BSData's (the option choices' pts) is compared. The Shield-Captain cases build the Shield-Captain, Shadowkeepers and Priority Assets under ids no committed export has shown (checked absent from NR_IDS), so each resolves by its exact name. The Meganobz case makes Orks catalogued for the case only: two datasheets, their costs and composition from GW's pages, the WARGEAR OPTIONS for the choices the export makes typed from the page, the weapons' keywords the built-in list Simple but effective has; its Warboss in Mega Armour alone (no attachment, no enhancement) as Warlord, its 6 Meganobz' models named Meganob as GW's composition names them.
